# Software Requirements Specification (SRS)
## Black Start Capability Plan (BCP) Management System

**Document Version:** 1.0  
**Date:** 2023-10-27  
**Status:** Draft for Review  
**Prepared for:** California Independent System Operator (CAISO)  
**Prepared by:** [Your Organization/Department Name]

---

### 1. Introduction

#### 1.1 Purpose
This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document defines the functional and non-functional requirements for a system to support the administration, planning, testing, and compliance tracking of the CAISO Black Start Capability Plan (BCP). The purpose of this system is to provide a centralized, reliable platform for managing all aspects of Black Start resource assurance in alignment with WECC and NERC reliability standards.

#### 1.2 Document Conventions
*   **Requirements IDs:** Functional requirements are prefixed with `FR-` and non-functional requirements with `NFR-`.
*   **Priority:** `(H)` High, `(M)` Medium, `(L)` Low.
*   **Keywords:** `SHALL`, `SHOULD`, `MAY`, `WILL` are used as defined in IETF RFC 2119.

#### 1.3 Intended Audience and Reading Suggestions
*   **CAISO Project Sponsors & Management:** For scope approval and high-level feature alignment.
*   **System Architects & Developers:** For designing and implementing the system based on detailed requirements.
*   **Quality Assurance Team:** For creating test plans and validation procedures.
*   **End Users (Planners, Operators, Test Administrators):** For understanding system capabilities and providing feedback.
*   **Compliance Auditors (WECC/NERC):** For understanding how the system supports regulatory compliance.

#### 1.4 Project Scope
The BCP Management System is a software platform designed to facilitate the planning, testing, record-keeping, training coordination, and compliance reporting for CAISO's Black Start resources. It serves as the system of record for all designated Black Start generators and the primary tool for managing the annual lifecycle of the BCP.

**In-Scope (System Support):**
*   Management of the Black Start generator database (capacity, location, status, test history).
*   Scheduling, tracking, and documenting results of mandatory Black Start unit tests.
*   Supporting annual planning studies by providing resource data and compliance status.
*   Managing the workflow for contract (RMR/Interim) establishment and review.
*   Tracking completion of annual operator restoration training and simulations.
*   Generating compliance reports for internal and external (WECC/NERC) audit purposes.

**Out-of-Scope:**
*   Real-time control systems for actual grid restoration during a blackout event.
*   Physical generator protection or control system design.
*   Day-to-day energy market bidding or scheduling functions.
*   Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) management software.
*   The system will not execute physical tests; it manages the administrative process surrounding them.

#### 1.5 References
*   WECC Reliability Standard: System Restoration (PLAN-SR-1)
*   NERC Reliability Standard: EOP-005-3 – System Restoration from Blackstart Resources
*   CAISO Tariff: Section 40 – Reliability Must-Run (RMR) Service
*   CAISO Business Practice Manual (BPM) for Reliability Requirements

### 2. Overall Description

#### 2.1 Product Perspective
The BCP Management System is a new, standalone application within the CAISO enterprise architecture. It will integrate with existing systems through defined interfaces:
*   **Generator Data Source:** To import basic generator characteristics and ownership data.
*   **CAISO Operator Training Simulator (OTS):** To schedule training sessions and record participation (future dependent on simulator availability).
*   **Document Management System (DMS):** To archive test reports, contracts, and audit documentation.
*   **External Portal:** For secure data submission by Generator Owners.

#### 2.2 Product Functions (High-Level)
1.  **Generator Portfolio Management:** Maintain a master database of all Black Start designated units.
2.  **Test Lifecycle Management:** Administer the end-to-end process for scheduling, executing, documenting, and analyzing Black Start tests.
3.  **Planning & Analysis Support:** Provide data and tools to assist Grid Planners in annual contingency studies and resource adequacy verification.
4.  **Compliance & Reporting:** Track compliance metrics, generate standard reports, and support audit requests.
5.  **Training Administration:** Schedule, track attendance, and manage materials for annual operator restoration training.
6.  **Contract Management Workflow:** Track the status of RMR and Interim contracts related to Black Start services.

#### 2.3 User Classes and Characteristics
| User Class | Characteristics | Key Needs |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **CAISO Grid Planner** | Power systems engineer. Uses planning tools. Needs accurate, current data. | Access to unit capabilities, test history, and location data for studies. Ability to mark units for annual review. |
| **CAISO Real-time Dispatcher** | Certified grid operator. Works in control room under time pressure. | Clear view of unit test schedules and status. Simple interface to request/dispatch tests. Access to unit start-up time limits. |
| **Generator Owner/Operator** | External entity. Varying levels of IT sophistication. | Secure portal to submit test data and documentation. Clear instructions on requirements and schedules. |
| **CAISO Test Administrator** | Operations support staff. Detail-oriented. Manages process compliance. | Dashboard to monitor all test activities. Workflow to review, validate, and record test results. Tools to calculate availability. |
| **Compliance Auditor (WECC/NERC)** | External regulator. Focused on evidence and traceability. | Read-only access to generate standardized compliance reports. Ability to drill down to source documentation (test reports, contracts). |
| **System Administrator** | IT staff. Manages user access and system health. | Tools for user role management, system configuration, and log monitoring. |

#### 2.4 Operating Environment
*   **Software:** Web-based application accessible via standard browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox). Backend built on Java/.NET/Node.js stack. Relational database (Oracle, PostgreSQL).
*   **Hardware:** Hosted on CAISO's secure internal servers or approved cloud environment (e.g., AWS GovCloud, Azure Government).
*   **Networks:** Accessible via CAISO corporate intranet. External access for Generator Owners via a secure, authenticated portal over HTTPS.

#### 2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints
1.  **Security:** System SHALL comply with CAISO cybersecurity policies and NERC CIP standards. All external data exchanges SHALL be encrypted.
2.  **Data Retention:** Test records, contracts, and compliance reports SHALL be retained for a minimum of seven years, per regulatory requirements.
3.  **Availability:** The system SHALL maintain 99.5% operational availability during business hours (0600-2000 PT).
4.  **Integration:** The system SHALL use CAISO-approved enterprise service bus (ESB) or API gateways for all system-to-system integrations.
5.  **Auditability:** All data changes (CRUD operations) for compliance-related entities (units, tests, contracts) SHALL be logged with user ID, timestamp, and change detail.

#### 2.6 Assumptions and Dependencies
*   **Assumption:** Generator Owners will have internet access and basic capability to upload documents via a web portal.
*   **Assumption:** Accurate and timely generator characteristic data will be available from the source system.
*   **Dependency:** Finalization of the "failure to start" percentage parameter by CAISO management for planning studies.
*   **Dependency:** Availability and schedule of the system simulator for integrated operator training exercises.

### 3. System Features and Requirements

#### 3.1 Feature: Black Start Generator Database Management
**Description:** Maintain a centralized, authoritative database of all generators designated for Black Start service.

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **FR-010** | The system SHALL allow authorized users (Test Admins, Planners) to create, read, update, and deactivate records for Black Start generators. | H |
| **FR-011** | Each generator record SHALL store: Unique ID, Name, Owner, Location (GPS/Bus), Technology Type, Certified Capacity (MW), Contract Type (RMR/Interim/Voluntary), Designation Date, and Status (Active/Inactive/Under Review). | H |
| **FR-012** | The system SHALL maintain a full version history for each generator record, capturing all changes to critical fields. | M |
| **FR-013** | The system SHALL provide filtered views and search capabilities for users to find generators by criteria such as location, technology, contract type, or test status. | M |

#### 3.2 Feature: Test Lifecycle Management
**Description:** Manage the end-to-end process for mandatory Black Start capability tests.

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **FR-020** | The system SHALL allow the Test Administrator to generate an annual test schedule, targeting at least one-third of RMR/Interim units, respecting constraints (e.g., no hydro tests during water constraints). | H |
| **FR-021** | The system SHALL allow a Real-time Dispatcher to request a test for a specific unit, logging the request time and operator. | H |
| **FR-022** | The system SHALL provide a portal for Generator Owners to submit test results, including: Test Date/Time, Start-up Time, Synchronization Time, Max Capacity Achieved, Ambient Temperature, and a signed test report (PDF). | H |
| **FR-023** | The system SHALL automatically calculate the unit's "availability" based on submitted start-up/sync times against technology-specific limits (e.g., 30 min for gas, 2.5 hours for hot steam). | H |
| **FR-024** | The system SHALL enforce a workflow where the Test Administrator must review and officially "Certify" or "Fail" a submitted test. | H |
| **FR-025** | For failed tests, the system SHALL require the Generator Owner to submit a root cause explanation and a corrective action plan via the portal. | H |
| **FR-026** | The system SHALL track the next required test date for each unit based on its last successful test date (not to exceed 5 years). | M |

#### 3.3 Feature: Planning & Compliance Support
**Description:** Provide tools and data to support annual planning and demonstrate compliance.

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **FR-030** | The system SHALL generate a standard annual report confirming that Black Start resources meet WECC restoration needs, incorporating current unit data and status. | H |
| **FR-031** | The system SHALL provide Grid Planners with an export function to extract generator data (location, capacity, availability) for use in external contingency study tools. | H |
| **FR-032** | The system SHALL maintain a dashboard showing key performance indicators (KPIs): % of units tested YTD, % of tests passed, overall plan compliance status. | M |
| **FR-033** | The system SHALL allow Compliance Auditors to generate on-demand reports listing all units, their test history for a given period, and certification status. | H |

#### 3.4 Feature: Training Administration
**Description:** Coordinate and track annual system restoration training for CAISO operators.

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **FR-040** | The system SHALL allow an administrator to schedule training sessions (classroom, simulation) and define a roster of required attendees. | M |
| **FR-041** | The system SHALL track operator attendance and mark training as "Completed" for each individual on their record. | M |
| **FR-042** | The system SHALL alert management and the individual operator if annual training is nearing its due date or is overdue. | L |

### 4. External Interface Requirements

#### 4.1 User Interfaces
*   **Primary UI:** A responsive, web-based interface with role-based dashboards.
*   **Generator Portal:** A simplified, branded external interface for data submission by Generator Owners.
*   **Reports UI:** A dedicated module for generating and downloading pre-formatted reports (PDF, Excel).

#### 4.2 Hardware Interfaces
*   None specified. The system is software-based.

#### 4.3 Software Interfaces
*   **SI-01: Corporate Generator Database:** SOAP/REST API to periodically synchronize basic generator static data (ID, Name, Location, Technology).
*   **SI-02: Document Management System (DMS):** API to deposit finalized, certified test reports and contracts for long-term archival.
*   **SI-03: Training Simulator (Future):** Interface to exchange schedule and attendance data (format and protocol TBD based on simulator).

#### 4.4 Communications Interfaces
*   All external communications (especially with the Generator Portal) SHALL use TLS 1.2 or higher.
*   The system SHALL support email notifications for workflow events (e.g., test request sent, results submitted, certification complete).

### 5. Non-Functional Requirements

#### 5.1 Performance Requirements
*   **Response Time:** 95% of all user interface interactions SHALL complete in less than 2 seconds under normal load.
*   **Report Generation:** Standard compliance reports SHALL be generated within 30 seconds.
*   **Concurrent Users:** The system SHALL support up to 50 concurrent active users.

#### 5.2 Safety Requirements
*   The system SHALL not issue direct control commands to generators. All test dispatches are requests that must be manually actioned by plant personnel.
*   The system SHALL clearly display safety warnings and operational constraints (e.g., "Hydro test not permitted during declared water constraint") to users scheduling tests.

#### 5.3 Security Requirements
*   Authentication SHALL integrate with CAISO's central Active Directory/LDAP.
*   Authorization SHALL be role-based (RBAC) with permissions defined per the user classes in Section 2.3.
*   All sensitive data at rest (e.g., test reports) SHALL be encrypted.
*   The system SHALL undergo annual security vulnerability assessments.

#### 5.4 Software Quality Attributes
*   **Reliability:** Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) > 720 hours.
*   **Maintainability:** Code SHALL adhere to CAISO development standards and include documentation for all core functions.
*   **Usability:** The system SHALL achieve a System Usability Scale (SUS) score of >75 after initial user training.
*   **Availability:** 99.5% availability during core business hours (0600-2000 PT), as per constraint 2.5.

### 6. Other Requirements

#### 6.1 Appendices
*   **Appendix A: Glossary**
    *   **Black Start:** The ability of a generating unit to start without an external electrical supply.
    *   **Cranking Path:** A designated transmission path used to energize the grid from a Black Start unit.
    *   **RMR (Reliability Must-Run):** A contractually obligated generator required for grid reliability.
    *   **WECC/NERC:** Western Electricity Coordinating Council / North American Electric Reliability Corporation.
*   **Appendix B: Data Models** *(To be developed during design phase)*
*   **Appendix C: Detailed Report Specifications** *(To be developed during design phase)*

#### 6.2 Undecided Issues (TBD)
1.  The specific system parameter for "Expected Failure to Start Percentage" (`FR-030` dependency).
2.  The technical interface specification for integration with the Operator Training Simulator (`SI-03`).
3.  The negotiation protocol and data fields for handling Black Start units in another Reliability Coordinator's area.

SRS: # Short Summary: Black Start Capability Plan (BCP)

## Background and Objectives
The Black Start Capability Plan (BCP) ensures the CAISO grid has sufficient, properly located Black Start generators to restore power after a major blackout. Its objective is to establish a reliable system restoration capability through planning, testing, and coordination in alignment with WECC and NERC requirements.

## In Scope
*   Annual planning to verify the quantity, size, availability, and location of Black Start units meet WECC restoration requirements.
*   Mandatory periodic testing (simulation or operational) for designated Black Start units to validate self-start and grid-support capabilities.
*   Maintaining a database of all designated Black Start generators, including their capacity, test status, and location.
*   Annual training for CAISO Real-time Grid Operators on system restoration procedures and Black Start unit coordination.
*   Establishing and managing contracts (RMR and Interim) with generators to secure Black Start services.

## Out of Scope
*   Generators that can only safely reject load down to their auxiliary load (a different form of Black Start aid).
*   Detailed operational processes for executing a system restoration during an actual event.
*   Specific technical designs for generator protection or control systems.
*   Day-to-day market operations and scheduling outside of test scenarios.
*   Environmental or safety compliance procedures for generator operations.

## Stakeholders and Core Use Cases
*   **CAISO Grid Planners**: Determine required Black Start capacity and location through contingency studies and annual planning evaluations.
*   **CAISO Real-time Operators (Dispatcher)**: Execute Black Start tests and coordinate restoration using designated units during an event.
*   **Generator Owners/Operators (RMR/Interim/Voluntary)**: Maintain and demonstrate their unit's Black Start capability through testing as required.
*   **CAISO Operations Support Test Administrator**: Administers the Black Start testing process, analyzes results, and updates unit availability records.
*   **WECC/NERC**: Review and audit CAISO's Black Start plans, documentation, and test results for regional reliability compliance.
*   **Transmission Owners (PTOs)**: Coordinate on cranking paths and system restoration plans with the CAISO.

**Core User Stories:**
1.  As a **CAISO Grid Planner**, I want to conduct annual contingency studies so that the Black Start resources are sufficient and correctly located for system restoration.
2.  As a **CAISO Real-time Dispatcher**, I want to dispatch a Black Start test for an RMR unit so that its operational readiness can be verified.
3.  As a **Generator Owner**, I want to perform and document a Black Start test every five years so that my unit maintains its certified status with the CAISO.
4.  As the **CAISO Test Administrator**, I want to receive the Black Start test results and ambient temperature data so that I can accurately calculate and record the unit's availability.
5.  As a **WECC Auditor**, I want to request and review CAISO's Black Start test documentation so that I can verify compliance with regional reliability standards.
6.  As a **CAISO Operator**, I want to participate in annual restoration training and simulations so that I am prepared to execute the Black Start plan during an emergency.

## Success Metrics
*   **100% compliance** with the requirement to annually verify that Black Start resources meet WECC restoration plan needs.
*   **Successful testing** of at least one-third of all RMR and Interim Black Start units annually, as requested by the CAISO.
*   **Annual completion** of system restoration training for all Real-time Grid Operators, including simulation exercises.

## Major Constraints
*   Black Start tests for hydroelectric units cannot be requested during periods of constrained water availability.
*   Units must meet strict start-up and synchronizing time limits based on their technology (e.g., 30 minutes for hydro/gas turbines, 2.5 hours for hot steam turbines).
*   Testing must not endanger personnel, damage equipment, harm the environment, or violate any laws or operating limits.
*   The plan and its associated database must be reviewed and updated at least every five years.
*   Generator owners must submit test failure explanations and correction plans to the CAISO.

## Undecided Issues
*   The specific percentage of Black Start units expected to fail to start during a restoration event (to be determined by the CAISO for studies).
*   Start time limits for Black Start facilities using unspecified technologies or located in another reliability coordinator's area are subject to negotiation.
*   The full implementation schedule for using a system simulator for operator training is dependent on simulator availability.

# Software Requirements Specification (SRS)
## For the I-15 Reversible Lane Control System (RLCS) Application Software

**Document Version:** 1.0  
**Date:** [Date of Generation]  
**Status:** Draft for Review  
**Prepared for:** [Client/Organization Name]  
**Prepared by:** [Your Company/Team Name]

---

### 1. Introduction

#### 1.1 Purpose
This document defines the functional and non-functional requirements for the I-15 Reversible Lane Control System (RLCS) Application Software. It serves as a formal agreement between the stakeholders and the development team, providing a comprehensive description of the system to be developed. The intended audience includes project managers, software developers, testers, system integrators, and all stakeholders identified in Section 3.

#### 1.2 Scope
The RLCS Application Software is a new system designed to replace an aging control system. Its primary purpose is to safely and reliably monitor and control field devices (gates, pop-up barriers, Changeable Message Signs (CMS), and lane control lights) to manage reversible lanes on the I-15 corridor during peak traffic periods and special events.

**In-Scope Elements:**
*   Development of the core RLCS application software.
*   Design and implementation of a Graphical User Interface (GUI) for operators and administrators.
*   Integration with new field controllers and their associated I/O cards via provided driver software.
*   Provision of real-time system status data to external traffic management systems via a dedicated external server interface.
*   Implementation of scheduled operations (automatic opening/closing sequences).
*   Configuration management for system parameters, users, and devices.

**Out-of-Scope Elements:**
*   Procurement, installation, and hardware configuration of field devices, controllers, and network infrastructure.
*   Development of underlying Operating Systems (OS), Database Management Systems (DBMS), or commercial reporting engines (COTS solutions will be used).
*   Design or implementation of the physical communications network.
*   Manual field operations that do not require software intervention.
*   Long-term data archival beyond the operational retention periods defined in this document.

#### 1.3 Definitions, Acronyms, and Abbreviations
| Term | Definition |
| :--- | :--- |
| **ATIS** | Advanced Traveler Information Systems |
| **ATMS** | Advanced Traffic Management System |
| **CMS** | Changeable Message Sign |
| **COTS** | Commercial Off-The-Shelf |
| **GUI** | Graphical User Interface |
| **I/O** | Input/Output |
| **RLCS** | Reversible Lane Control System |
| **SRS** | Software Requirements Specification |

#### 1.4 References
*   [Reference to any existing project charter, concept of operations, or interface control documents]
*   [Reference to relevant traffic safety standards, e.g., MUTCD, local DOT standards]

#### 1.5 Overview
The remainder of this document is structured as follows: Section 2 provides a general description of the product. Section 3 identifies all stakeholders and users. Section 4 details specific system requirements, including functional, interface, and non-functional requirements. Appendices contain supplementary information.

### 2. Overall Description

#### 2.1 Product Perspective
The RLCS Application Software is a new, self-contained component within the larger I-15 Reversible Lane infrastructure. It will interface with several external systems:
*   **Field Device Controllers:** To send control commands and receive status/health data.
*   **External Data Server:** To publish lane status and system health data for consumption by ATMS, ValuePricing, and ATIS.
*   **COTS Database:** For storing configuration, event logs, and historical data.
*   **Operator Workstations:** Where the GUI will be hosted.

It is intended to replace the legacy system, offering improved reliability, configurability, and integration capabilities.

#### 2.2 Product Functions (Summary)
The core functions of the RLCS software include:
1.  **Device Monitoring:** Continuously poll and display the real-time status of all field devices.
2.  **Lane Control:** Execute safe, sequenced commands to open or close reversible lanes, either manually (operator-initiated) or automatically (scheduled).
3.  **Alarm Management:** Detect device faults, communication failures, and safety rule violations, and present them to the operator with appropriate priority.
4.  **User Management:** Provide role-based access control for all system functions.
5.  **Configuration Management:** Allow authorized users to configure devices, schedules, user accounts, and system parameters.
6.  **Reporting:** Generate standard and ad-hoc reports on system operations, alarms, and events.
7.  **Data Provisioning:** Securely transmit system state information to designated external systems.

#### 2.3 User Characteristics
| User Class | Skill Level | Key Responsibilities |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Operator** | Proficient in traffic ops | Daily control of lanes, monitoring status, responding to alarms. |
| **System Administrator** | IT/Traffic Systems Expert | User account management, system configuration, mode changes. |
| **Field Maintenance Staff** | Technical/Field Engineer | Perform maintenance mode operations from remote terminals. |
| **Management** | Non-Technical/Managerial | Review historical reports and high-level system status. |
| **Electrical Systems Staff** | Technical | Review hardware-specific reports and diagnostic data. |
| **Software Systems Staff** | Technical | Review software-related logs and system performance data. |

#### 2.4 Constraints
1.  **Operational:** The system must operate 24/7/365 with a maximum recovery time objective (RTO) of 10 minutes following any failure.
2.  **Technical:** The database and reporting layer must be implemented using approved COTS products.
3.  **Safety:** The software must enforce strict safety interlocks to prevent the simultaneous opening of entrances for opposing traffic flows.
4.  **Maintainability:** The system must be designed to accommodate future roadway changes (e.g., adding new gates) through configuration table updates, without requiring source code modifications.
5.  **Security:** All communications between the central system and field controllers must use wired, secure connections; wireless communication is prohibited.

#### 2.5 Assumptions and Dependencies
*   It is assumed that the field hardware (controllers, I/O cards, devices) and their driver software will be provided and will conform to specified interface protocols.
*   The system depends on the stability and availability of the underlying OS, network, and COTS database/reporting software.
*   Final requirements for polling intervals and communication rates are dependent on the selected field controller model's capabilities.

### 3. Stakeholder and User Requirements

#### 3.1 Stakeholder Identification
See Section 2.3 for detailed user characteristics.

#### 3.2 Core Use Cases
1.  **UC-01: Execute Manual Lane Reversal**
    *   **Actor:** Operator
    *   **Description:** Operator initiates a safe, sequenced opening or closing of the reversible lanes outside of scheduled times.
2.  **UC-02: Configure System Security**
    *   **Actor:** System Administrator
    *   **Description:** Admin creates/modifies/deletes user accounts and assigns roles/permissions to control system access.
3.  **UC-03: Perform Remote Maintenance Operation**
    *   **Actor:** Field Maintenance Staff
    *   **Description:** Staff places the system or a device subset into maintenance mode and executes test or repair sequences from a field terminal.
4.  **UC-04: Generate Historical Performance Report**
    *   **Actor:** Management
    *   **Description:** User selects a date range and generates a report detailing system availability, operation success/failure rates, and alarm history.
5.  **UC-05: Monitor Real-Time System Status**
    *   **Actor:** Operator
    *   **Description:** The GUI continuously updates to show device states (e.g., gate position, light color) and triggers visual/audible alarms for any faults.
6.  **UC-06: Provide Lane Status to External System**
    *   **Actor:** External System (e.g., ATMS)
    *   **Description:** The RLCS external server makes current lane status (OPEN/CLOSED/TRANSITION) available via a defined API for polling by authorized external systems.

### 4. System Requirements

#### 4.1 Functional Requirements

##### 4.1.1 User Interface (GUI) Requirements
*   **FR-GUI-01:** The GUI shall provide a schematic map view of the reversible lane corridor, displaying the real-time status of all monitored devices.
*   **FR-GUI-02:** The GUI shall provide a dedicated control panel for operators to initiate **Open Sequence**, **Close Sequence**, **Halt**, and **Override** commands.
*   **FR-GUI-03:** The GUI shall include an alarm banner/panel that lists active alarms, sorted by priority (Critical, Major, Minor), and updates within **2 seconds** of detection.
*   **FR-GUI-04:** The GUI shall require user authentication via login and enforce role-based permissions for all control and configuration functions.

##### 4.1.2 Control and Monitoring Requirements
*   **FR-CONTROL-01:** The system shall execute a pre-defined, sequential set of commands to field devices to transition lanes from "Closed" to "Open" (and vice-versa).
*   **FR-CONTROL-02:** The system shall poll the status of all field devices at a configurable interval (to be determined based on hardware).
*   **FR-CONTROL-03:** The system shall compare device command feedback with expected states and generate an alarm on any mismatch.
*   **FR-SAFETY-01:** The system shall implement a configurable safety interlock rule to physically prevent the "Open" command from being sent to entrances for opposing directions simultaneously.

##### 4.1.3 Scheduling Requirements
*   **FR-SCHED-01:** The system shall allow an administrator to create and store weekly schedules for standard opening and closing operations.
*   **FR-SCHED-02:** The system shall automatically initiate scheduled opening and closing sequences without operator intervention.
*   **FR-SCHED-03:** The system shall support configuration of special event schedules that override the standard weekly schedule.

##### 4.1.4 Reporting Requirements
*   **FR-REP-01:** The system shall log all operator commands, system actions, device state changes, and alarms with a timestamp and user ID.
*   **FR-REP-02:** The system shall generate a standard "Daily Operations Log" report.
*   **FR-REP-03:** The system shall allow users to generate ad-hoc reports based on filterable criteria (date, device, alarm type, etc.) using the COTS reporting tool.

##### 4.1.5 Configuration Management Requirements
*   **FR-CONFIG-01:** The system shall provide forms/tables for administrators to configure: User accounts and roles, Field device parameters, Safety interlock rules, and Communication settings.
*   **FR-CONFIG-02:** All configuration changes shall be logged and require administrator-level authentication.

##### 4.1.6 External Interface Requirements
*   **FR-EXT-01:** The system shall provide lane status (OPEN, CLOSED, IN TRANSITION, FAULT) to an external server module.
*   **FR-EXT-02:** The external server shall make this data available via a secure, documented API (e.g., RESTful web service or message queue).

#### 4.2 Non-Functional Requirements

##### 4.2.1 Performance Requirements
*   **NFR-PERF-01:** The system shall achieve **99.99%** operational availability annually.
*   **NFR-PERF-02:** The GUI shall reflect device status updates and alarm conditions within **2 seconds** of the system detecting the change.
*   **NFR-PERF-03:** The system shall be capable of successfully executing a minimum of **four** scheduled opening/closing sequences per day.

##### 4.2.2 Reliability & Availability Requirements
*   **NFR-REL-01:** The system shall be designed for 24/7 operation.
*   **NFR-REL-02:** In the event of a software failure, the system shall be capable of restarting and resuming normal operations within a **10-minute** recovery time objective.

##### 4.2.3 Security Requirements
*   **NFR-SEC-01:** All user access shall be controlled by username/password authentication.
*   **NFR-SEC-02:** Communications between the central system and field controllers shall be via secure, wired protocols only.
*   **NFR-SEC-03:** User permissions shall follow a role-based access control (RBAC) model.

##### 4.2.4 Maintainability Requirements
*   **NFR-MAIN-01:** The system shall be designed so that changes to roadway geometry or device additions can be managed through configuration updates, without modifying application source code.

#### 4.3 Interface Requirements
*   **IR-01:** **Field Controller Interface:** The software shall communicate via a protocol defined by the selected controller's driver software (e.g., Modbus TCP, DNP3, proprietary API). *[Specific model TBD]*.
*   **IR-02:** **Database Interface:** The application shall connect to a relational database (e.g., Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL) using standard ODBC/JDBC connectors.
*   **IR-03:** **External System API:** The external server shall provide data in a standard format (e.g., JSON, XML) over HTTPS or a dedicated message bus.

### 5. Appendices

#### 5.1 Undecided Issues (To Be Resolved)
1.  Selection of the specific intelligent field controller model.
2.  Final choice of COTS database and reporting software (e.g., Oracle Database, Microsoft SQL Server Reporting Services, Crystal Reports).
3.  Detailed specification of all input validation checks and abnormal situation handling sequences.
4.  Exact configurable timer values for override commands and sequence halt scenarios.
5.  Finalized network communication rates and device polling intervals, pending hardware selection.

#### 5.2 Data Retention Policy
*   System event and alarm logs shall be retained online for a minimum of **90 days**.
*   Historical data for reporting shall be retained for a minimum of **2 years**.
*   Configuration change history shall be retained for the life of the system.

---
**Document Approval:**

| Role | Name | Signature | Date |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Project Sponsor | | | |
| Lead Systems Engineer | | | |
| Software Development Manager | | | |
| Quality Assurance Manager | | | |

The I-15 RLCS Application Software will replace an aging system to control reversible lanes during peak traffic and special events. # Software Requirements Specification (SRS)
## Publications Management System (PMS)

**Document Version:** 1.0
**Date:** [Current Date]
**Status:** Draft for Review

---

### 1. Introduction

#### 1.1 Purpose
This document defines the functional and non-functional requirements for the Publications Management System (PMS). It is intended for use by the project stakeholders, developers, testers, and project managers to ensure a common understanding of the system to be developed.

#### 1.2 Scope
The PMS is a web-based platform for managing a database of academic publications. Its core purpose is to provide controlled access to bibliographic information and full-text documents for users within the Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) network and registered members. The system will support publication upload, search, viewing, and download functionalities through both web and command-line interfaces.

**In-Scope Features:**
*   Web and command-line interfaces (CLI) for system interaction.
*   User registration, authentication, and role-based access control.
*   Publication search, viewing metadata, and downloading full-text documents (PDF, PostScript).
*   Upload and editing of publications with automatic metadata extraction from supported formats.
*   Administrative and moderator functions for user, group, and publication management.

**Out-of-Scope Features:**
*   Support for document formats other than PDF, PostScript, BibTeX, and RIS (e.g., MS Word).
*   Automatic disambiguation of author or institute name aliases.
*   Management of audio or video files.
*   Automated retrieval of full-text documents from URLs provided in abstracts.
*   Extension of services to non-academic or external user bases beyond the VUB network.

#### 1.3 Definitions, Acronyms, and Abbreviations
*   **PMS:** Publications Management System.
*   **VUB:** Vrije Universiteit Brussel.
*   **BibTeX:** A bibliographic data format.
*   **RIS:** Research Information Systems format, a standardized tag format for bibliographic citations.
*   **RDoc:** Ruby Documentation system.
*   **W3C:** World Wide Web Consortium.
*   **XHTML:** Extensible HyperText Markup Language.
*   **CLI:** Command-Line Interface.
*   **GUI:** Graphical User Interface (Web Interface).

#### 1.4 References
*   W3C XHTML 1.0 Transitional Specification.
*   Ruby Programming Language Documentation.
*   RDoc User Guide.

#### 1.5 Overview
The remainder of this document is structured as follows: Section 2 provides an overall description of the product, its users, and constraints. Section 3 details the specific functional and non-functional requirements. Appendices may contain supplementary information.

### 2. Overall Description

#### 2.1 Product Perspective
The PMS is a new, self-contained system to be deployed on the existing Linux-based Wilma server at VUB. It will interact with users via a web browser (rendering XHTML) and a command-line shell. It will manage its own database of users, publications, and metadata.

#### 2.2 User Classes and Characteristics
| User Class | Description | Key Characteristics |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Guest** | An anonymous user accessing from outside the VUB network. | Very limited access; can only view the login/registration page. |
| **VUB-Network User** | A user connected from within the VUB IP range, not necessarily logged in. | Can search the publication database and download available full-text documents. |
| **Member** | A logged-in user with a registered account. | Inherits VUB-Network User privileges; can manage personal account details. |
| **Publisher** | A logged-in Member with elevated privileges. | Can upload new publications (single/bulk), edit metadata for their own publications. |
| **Moderator** | A privileged user responsible for content quality. | Can edit publication details for assigned departments/groups, manage user levels and group permissions within their scope. |
| **Administrator** | A super-user with full system oversight. | Has full control over all users, groups, publications, and system configuration settings. |

#### 2.3 Operating Environment
*   **Server:** Must operate on the VUB's Linux-based Wilma server.
*   **Software Stack:** Must be implemented in Ruby without the use of frameworks (e.g., Rails, Sinatra). Only free software libraries and tools are permitted.
*   **Web Standard:** The web interface must generate pages compliant with W3C XHTML 1.0 Transitional.
*   **Documentation:** Source code must be documented using RDoc.

#### 2.4 Design and Implementation Constraints
1.  **Technical:** Implementation in plain Ruby, no external frameworks.
2.  **Legal:** Use of free/open-source software libraries only.
3.  **Architectural:** Design must be modular to allow for future expansion of features.
4.  **Compliance:** Web output must validate against XHTML 1.0 Transitional standards.

#### 2.5 Assumptions and Dependencies
*   The Wilma server provides a stable Linux environment with Ruby installed.
*   Network access controls for identifying "VUB-Network Users" (via IP range) are handled by the server environment.
*   Success metrics related to Wilma server downtime are outside the direct control of the PMS application.

### 3. Specific Requirements

#### 3.1 Functional Requirements

**3.1.1 User Management (UM)**
*   **UM-1:** The system shall allow a Guest to register for a new account by providing required details (e.g., name, email, password).
*   **UM-2:** The system shall allow users (Member, Publisher, Moderator, Administrator) to authenticate using a username/email and password.
*   **UM-3:** The system shall enforce role-based privileges as defined in Section 2.2.
*   **UM-4:** The system shall allow a Member to view and edit their own account profile information.
*   **UM-5:** The system shall allow an Administrator to create, view, edit, and delete any user account.
*   **UM-6:** The system shall allow an Administrator and Moderator to assign users to groups and manage group permissions.

**3.1.2 Publication Management (PM)**
*   **PM-1:** The system shall allow a Publisher to upload a new publication. The upload must include the full-text document (PDF/PS) and/or a metadata file (BibTeX/RIS).
*   **PM-2:** The system shall automatically extract and store metadata from uploaded BibTeX or RIS files.
*   **PM-3:** The system shall allow a Publisher to edit the metadata of publications they have uploaded.
*   **PM-4:** The system shall allow a Moderator to edit the metadata of publications belonging to their assigned department or group.
*   **PM-5:** The system shall allow an Administrator to edit or delete any publication.
*   **PM-6:** The system shall support bulk upload of publications by Publishers (e.g., via a ZIP file containing multiple BibTeX/files).

**3.1.3 Search and Retrieval (SR)**
*   **SR-1:** The system shall provide a search interface for VUB-Network Users, Members, Publishers, Moderators, and Administrators.
*   **SR-2:** The search function shall allow filtering by keyword(s), author name, title, year, and other relevant bibliographic fields.
*   **SR-3:** The system shall display search results in a list, showing core metadata (title, authors, year, source).
*   **SR-4:** The system shall allow users to view the full metadata record of a publication from the search results.
*   **SR-5:** The system shall allow VUB-Network Users and all logged-in roles to download the full-text document (PDF/PS) of a publication, if available.

**3.1.4 Interface Requirements (IR)**
*   **IR-1:** The system shall provide a web-based GUI accessible via standard browsers.
*   **IR-2:** The web GUI shall render valid XHTML 1.0 Transitional.
*   **IR-3:** The system shall provide a CLI for executing administrative and batch operations (e.g., bulk imports, user management scripts).

#### 3.2 Non-Functional Requirements

**3.2.1 Performance**
*   **PER-1:** The system shall have an availability of >99% during standard operational hours, excluding downtime of the underlying Wilma server.
*   **PER-2:** The automatic metadata extraction process shall succeed for at least 95% of submitted BibTeX/RIS files.
*   *Note: Specific response times and concurrent user handling are TBD (To Be Determined).*

**3.2.2 Usability**
*   **USA-1:** The system shall achieve a user satisfaction score of at least 4 out of 5 on ease of search and download functionality, as measured by post-deployment survey.

**3.2.3 Reliability**
*   The system shall maintain data integrity, ensuring no loss of publication data or user information under normal operating conditions.

**3.2.4 Security**
*   **SEC-1:** User passwords shall be stored using a strong, irreversible hashing algorithm.
*   **SEC-2:** Access to publication downloads shall be restricted as per the user role definitions (e.g., Guests cannot download).
*   **SEC-3:** The system shall be protected against common web vulnerabilities (e.g., SQL injection, cross-site scripting).

#### 3.3 Undecided / TBD Issues
The following items require further stakeholder discussion and specification:
1.  The maximum allowable file size for uploaded publication documents.
2.  Detailed performance requirements (e.g., "search results returned within X seconds under Y concurrent users").
3.  The final installation and deployment procedure on the Wilma server.
4.  Support for additional export formats for publication lists (beyond the core HTML, PDF, PS).
5.  The specific set of enhanced functionalities for the Administrator control panel.

---
*This document is considered a living specification and may be updated as requirements are clarified and the project evolves.*

# Software Requirements Specification (SRS)
## VII Data Use Analysis and Processing (DUAP) System
### Version 1.0

**Prepared for:** Michigan Department of Transportation (MDOT)
**Prepared by:** [Your Organization/Team Name]
**Date:** [Date]

---

## 1. Introduction

### 1.1 Purpose
This document defines the functional and non-functional requirements for the VII Data Use Analysis and Processing (DUAP) System. The DUAP system is a research prototype designed to evaluate the utility of Vehicle Infrastructure Integration (VII) data for enhancing transportation safety, mobility, and asset management. This SRS serves as a reference for developers, testers, project managers, and stakeholders, and will be used to guide the design, implementation, and verification of the system.

### 1.2 Document Conventions
*   **Requirements:** Functional requirements are labeled `FR-XXX`. Non-functional requirements are labeled `NFR-XXX`.
*   **Priority:** (H) High, (M) Medium, (L) Low.
*   **Keywords:** `MUST`, `SHALL`, `SHOULD`, `WILL`, `MAY` are used as defined in IETF RFC 2119.

### 1.3 Project Scope
The DUAP system is a functional prototype, not a production operational system. Its core purpose is to collect, consolidate, convert, and communicate VII and complementary transportation data to support operational decision-making demonstrations and application assessments.

**In-Scope:**
*   Collection of probe vehicle, traffic, weather, and road condition data from multiple sources, including the VII Proof of Concept network.
*   Processing of raw data via computational services to derive traffic metrics, detect incidents, and assess road conditions.
*   Dynamic (cached) storage for one week and persistent (archived) long-term storage of all data with geo-references and timestamps.
*   Publication of processed data and alerts in standard formats (e.g., SAE J2354) for consumption by external systems and internal presentation services.
*   Provision of role-based, web-based user interfaces for browsing traffic, incident, weather, and asset condition information.

**Out-of-Scope:**
*   Operational deployment as a 24/7 production system.
*   Collection of probe data from deferred sources (e.g., The Rapid, Ann Arbor Transit, DDOT, car rental fleets).
*   Direct publishing interfaces to specific traffic analysis tools (VISSIM, Synchro, Paramics, SimTraffic).
*   Guarantee of real-time data with zero latency.
*   Resolution of data privacy, ownership, and policy issues (these are external institutional requirements).

### 1.4 References
*   Michigan Department of Information Technology (MDIT) IT Standards.
*   SAE J2354 - Data Dictionary for Advanced Traveler Information Systems (ATIS).
*   Michigan Geographic Framework (MGF) Specifications.
*   VII Proof of Concept System Architecture Documentation.

## 2. Overall Description

### 2.1 Product Perspective
The DUAP system is a middleware and application layer component that sits between various transportation data sources and end-user applications. It ingests data, processes it, stores it, and makes it available for visualization and integration.

### 2.2 Product Functions (Summary)
1.  **Data Ingestion:** Acquire data from VII probe vehicles, traffic sensors, weather feeds, and road condition reports.
2.  **Data Processing:** Transform and analyze raw data to compute travel times, speeds, detect incidents, and identify road surface issues.
3.  **Data Storage:** Manage a short-term cache for operational data and a long-term archive for historical analysis.
4.  **Data Publication:** Expose processed data, alerts, and metrics via standard APIs and data feeds.
5.  **Data Visualization:** Provide web-based map and reporting interfaces for different stakeholder roles.

### 2.3 User Classes and Characteristics
| User Class | Characteristics | Key Needs |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Transportation Operator** | MDOT staff in TOC; needs timely, accurate situational awareness. | View real-time incidents, traffic flow, and alerts on a map. |
| **System Administrator** | IT staff responsible for system upkeep. | Configure data sources, monitor system health, manage users. |
| **Maintainer / Field Crew** | Roadway maintenance staff; often mobile. | Receive and view prioritized alerts (e.g., potholes) on a map or simple list. |
| **Asset Manager** | Planning staff; uses historical and condition data. | Access reports and summaries on road condition trends for planning. |
| **Researcher** | UMTRI or academic analyst; requires detailed data. | Query and export large sets of archived, geo-referenced raw and processed data. |
| **Traveler (Public)** | General public accessing a public website. | View current travel times, incidents, and construction for trip planning. |
| **Emergency Services** | Police, Fire, EMS dispatch. | Access incident data and traffic impact assessments. |

### 2.4 Operating Environment
*   **Software:** Java-based application server (e.g., Tomcat, JBoss), Oracle 11g/12c database, ESRI or open-source geospatial libraries compatible with MGF.
*   **Hardware:** Must run on MDIT-approved server infrastructure.
*   **Network:** Must operate within secured MDOT network zones, with controlled access to external data sources (VII network, weather APIs).

### 2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints
1.  `NFR-CON-001` (H): The system SHALL be developed using a Java foundation, in compliance with MDIT standards.
2.  `NFR-CON-002` (H): The system SHALL use an Oracle database for persistent storage.
3.  `NFR-CON-003` (H): All spatial data and geo-references SHALL use the Michigan Geographic Framework (MGF).
4.  `NFR-CON-004` (M): The system architecture SHALL be extensible to allow for the addition of new data source adapters and processing algorithms with minimal code changes.

### 2.6 Assumptions and Dependencies
*   **Assumption:** The VII Proof of Concept network and other defined data sources will be available and provide data in a consistent, albeit potentially changing, format.
*   **Assumption:** Data provided will be "near real-time"; applications consuming DUAP data are responsible for checking timestamps for suitability.
*   **Dependency:** Data quality flags from source systems (e.g., vehicle sensor calibration state) will be propagated and must be handled by downstream applications.
*   **Dependency:** System performance and data volume are dependent on external factors (e.g., penetration rate of VII-equipped vehicles).

## 3. System Features and Requirements

### 3.1 Data Ingestion Service
**Description:** This component is responsible for connecting to external data sources, receiving or fetching data, performing initial validation, and placing it into the processing pipeline.

**Requirements:**
*   `FR-ING-001` (H): The system SHALL accept VII probe data messages (BSM, TIM) from the VII Proof of Concept network interface.
*   `FR-ING-002` (H): The system SHALL ingest traffic data (e.g., volume, speed) from specified MDOT sensor sources (e.g., TOC feeds).
*   `FR-ING-003` (H): The system SHALL ingest weather data (e.g., precipitation, temperature) from designated weather service APIs.
*   `FR-ING-004` (M): The system SHALL provide a configuration interface (e.g., admin UI) to add, modify, or disable data source connections. *(Supports User Story #2)*
*   `FR-ING-005` (M): The system SHALL tag all ingested data with a source identifier, receipt timestamp, and original quality flags.

### 3.2 Data Processing & Computation Service
**Description:** This component transforms raw data into derived metrics and detects events of interest.

**Requirements:**
*   `FR-PRC-001` (H): The system SHALL compute link-based traffic metrics (e.g., average speed, travel time) from probe vehicle data.
*   `FR-PRC-002` (H): The system SHALL implement algorithms to automatically detect traffic incidents (e.g., sudden speed drops, congestion patterns) and generate incident alerts.
*   `FR-PRC-003` (H): The system SHALL process probe and other data to assess road surface conditions (e.g., detect potential potholes from vertical acceleration data) and generate condition alerts. *(Supports User Story #3)*
*   `FR-PRC-004` (M): The system SHALL fuse data from multiple sources (e.g., probe + fixed sensors) to improve metric accuracy where possible.
*   `FR-PRC-005` (L): The system MAY compute and store Origin/Destination (O/D) data, pending definition of specific O/D type.

### 3.3 Data Storage Service
**Description:** This component manages both short-term operational cache and long-term historical archive.

**Requirements:**
*   `FR-STR-001` (H): The system SHALL maintain a dynamic cache of processed data (metrics, alerts) for a minimum of seven (7) days for operational access.
*   `FR-STR-002` (H): The system SHALL persist all raw and processed data, with timestamps and MGF geo-references, to an archival database for long-term retention. *(Supports User Story #5)*
*   `FR-STR-003` (M): The archival storage SHALL support efficient time-range and spatial queries by the Researcher user class.

### 3.4 Data Publication & API Service
**Description:** This component provides standardized interfaces for internal and external systems to access DUAP data.

**Requirements:**
*   `FR-PUB-001` (H): The system SHALL publish processed traffic metrics, incident alerts, and road condition alerts in a standards-based format (e.g., compliant with SAE J2354 profiles).
*   `FR-PUB-002` (H): The system SHALL provide a RESTful API or web service for authenticated programmatic access to cached and archived data.
*   `FR-PUB-003` (M): Published data feeds SHALL include clear metadata indicating data latency, timestamp, and quality indicators.

### 3.5 Presentation & User Interface Service
**Description:** This component provides web-based visualizations and tools for different user roles.

**Requirements:**
*   `FR-UI-001` (H): The system SHALL provide a secure, map-based operational view for Transportation Operators to display real-time incidents, traffic speeds, and weather overlays. *(Supports User Story #1)*
*   `FR-UI-002` (H): The system SHALL provide a public, map-based traveler information website displaying current travel times, major incidents, and construction zones. *(Supports User Story #4)*
*   `FR-UI-003` (H): The system SHALL provide an interface for Maintainers to view and prioritize a list or map of generated road condition alerts (e.g., potholes). *(Supports User Story #3)*
*   `FR-UI-004` (M): The system SHALL provide a reporting interface for Asset Managers to generate and browse summaries of road condition trends over user-defined periods. *(Supports User Story #6)*
*   `FR-UI-005` (M): The system SHALL provide a tool for Researchers to query, filter, and export archived raw and processed data in common formats (CSV, Shapefile). *(Supports User Story #5)*
*   `FR-UI-006` (L): The interface MAY allow users to select units of measurement and manage map data layers.

## 4. Non-Functional Requirements

### 4.1 Performance Requirements
*   `NFR-PER-001`: The system SHALL process and make available ingested VII probe data with a latency of no more than 2 minutes from time of receipt 95% of the time ("near real-time").
*   `NFR-PER-002`: The public traveler website SHALL load the initial map view and data within 5 seconds under normal load conditions.
*   `NFR-PER-003`: The operational view SHALL update incident and traffic data on the map at intervals configurable by the user (e.g., every 30-120 seconds).

### 4.2 Safety & Security Requirements
*   `NFR-SEC-001`: The system SHALL implement role-based access control (RBAC) to restrict data and functions based on user classes (Operator, Admin, Researcher, Public).
*   `NFR-SEC-002`: All administrative functions and access to raw/archived data SHALL require authentication.
*   `NFR-SEC-003`: The system SHALL not store personally identifiable information (PII). Data linking probes to specific vehicle IDs SHALL be anonymized or excluded per policy.

### 4.3 Data Quality Requirements
*   `NFR-QUA-001`: The system SHALL propagate data quality flags from source systems through to published outputs and user interfaces.
*   `NFR-QUA-002`: The system SHALL log all data ingestion errors and processing failures for administrative review.

### 4.4 Usability Requirements
*   `NFR-USA-001`: The operational and maintenance interfaces SHALL be designed for use in a Transportation Operations Center (TOC) environment, with clear visual cues for alerts.
*   `NFR-USA-002`: The public traveler interface SHALL be designed for clarity and ease of use by the general public on standard web browsers.

## 5. Appendices

### 5.1 Glossary
*   **VII:** Vehicle Infrastructure Integration.
*   **Probe Data:** Data generated by vehicles, such as position, speed, heading, and vehicle state.
*   **BSM:** Basic Safety Message (SAE J2735).
*   **TIM:** Traveler Information Message (SAE J2735).
*   **MGF:** Michigan Geographic Framework.
*   **TOC:** Transportation Operations Center.
*   **O/D:** Origin/Destination.

### 5.2 Undecided and Deferred Issues
1.  The specific interface formats (protocol, schema) for many external data sources and output consumers are TBD during prototype design.
2.  Privacy policies for handling vehicle probe anonymity are externally governed and may impact certain research functionalities.
3.  Data ownership and use limitations from third-party sources (e.g., weather data) may impose constraints on DUAP's data redistribution.
4.  Implementation details for advanced UI features (unit selection, complex layer management) are deferred as low priority.

---
*Document End*

SRS: # Short Summary: VII Data Use Analysis and Processing (DUAP) System Requirements

## Background and Objectives
The DUAP system is a research prototype for the Michigan Department of Transportation (MDOT) to evaluate Vehicle Infrastructure Integration (VII) data's utility in enhancing safety, mobility, and asset management. Its objective is to collect, consolidate, convert, and communicate VII and other transportation data to support operational decisions and application demonstrations.

## In Scope
*   Collecting probe vehicle, traffic, weather, and road condition data from multiple sources, including the VII Proof of Concept network.
*   Processing data via computational services to derive traffic metrics, detect incidents, and assess road conditions.
*   Storing data dynamically (cached for one week) and persistently (archived) with geo-references and timestamps.
*   Publishing processed data and alerts in standard formats (e.g., SAE J2354) for external systems and internal presentation services.
*   Providing web-based user interfaces for browsing traffic, incident, weather, and asset condition information.

## Out of Scope
*   Operational deployment as a production system; it is a functional prototype for demonstration and assessment.
*   Collection of probe data from several transit agencies (e.g., The Rapid, Ann Arbor Transit, DDOT) and car rental fleets, which are deferred.
*   Publishing data to specific traffic analysis tools (VISSIM, Synchro, Paramics, SimTraffic), which are deferred.
*   Real-time data with zero latency; the system handles "near real-time" data with inherent delays.
*   Resolving data privacy, ownership, and policy issues, which are external institutional requirements.

## Stakeholders and Core Use Cases
**Stakeholders:**
*   **MDOT & Partner Transportation Agencies (Operators, Maintainers, Asset Managers):** Use data to minimize incident impact, maintain roadways, and manage assets cost-effectively.
*   **System Administrators:** Administer the DUAP system to ensure data availability.
*   **Transportation Agency Management & Contractors:** Supervise staff and perform contracted work using DUAP data.
*   **Travelers:** Obtain trip information for route planning and delay avoidance.
*   **Emergency Services:** Use data for incident response and impact assessment.
*   **Researchers/University Personnel (e.g., UMTRI):** Analyze data for transportation research.
*   **Michigan Transportation Research Board (MTRB):** Advises on research needs and direction.
*   **Automobile Manufacturers (OEMs) & VII Network Operators:** Provide vehicle data and operate the communication infrastructure.

**Core User Stories:**
1.  As a **Transportation Operator**, I want to view detected incidents and traffic conditions so that I can quickly assess and respond to events.
2.  As a **System Administrator**, I want to add or modify data input services so that I can integrate new data sources into the system.
3.  As a **Maintainer**, I want to receive alerts on pothole locations so that I can prioritize roadway repair tasks.
4.  As a **Traveler**, I want to access a public web interface showing travel times and incidents so that I can plan my route accordingly.
5.  As a **Researcher**, I want to access archived, geo-referenced probe data so that I can analyze traffic patterns and algorithm effectiveness.
6.  As an **Asset Manager**, I want to browse derived road condition reports so that I can inform annual program and project planning.

## Success Metrics
*   Successful integration and processing of VII probe data alongside traffic and weather data from specified sources.
*   Demonstrated utility of derived information (e.g., incident detection, travel time) for at least one operational application per key area (safety, mobility, asset management).
*   System meets specified performance and quality characteristics, including extensibility for adding new data sources and algorithms.

## Major Constraints
*   Must conform to Michigan Department of Information Technology (MDIT) IT standards, including using a Java foundation and Oracle database.
*   Must use Michigan Geographic Framework for all geo-references.
*   Data is "near real-time" with inherent latency; consuming systems must evaluate data suitability based on timestamps.
*   Data quality may vary due to vehicle sensor calibration states; applications must handle data quality flags.
*   Data volume and availability depend on external factors like the number of VII-equipped vehicles and roadside units.

## Undecided Issues
*   Specific interface formats for many external data sources and output consumers are to be determined during prototype design.
*   The ability to link probe data directly to specific vehicles for research poses unresolved privacy and anonymity policy issues.
*   Ownership and use limitations for commingled data from third-party sources may impact DUAP's usefulness.
*   The system's capability to collect Origin/Destination (O/D) data is noted, but the specific type of O/D data needs to be established.
*   Implementation details for certain presentation features (e.g., unit selection, data layer management) are deferred or marked as low priority.

# Software Requirements Specification (SRS)
## Puget Sound Moodle Enhancements Project

**Document Version:** 1.0
**Date:** October 26, 2023
**Status:** Draft for Review
**Prepared for:** University of Puget Sound
**Prepared by:** [Project Team/Consultant Name]

---

### 1. Introduction

#### 1.1 Purpose
This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document defines the functional and non-functional requirements for the enhancement of the Moodle Learning Management System (LMS) at the University of Puget Sound. The purpose is to provide a detailed description of the features to be developed, serving as a contractual agreement between stakeholders and the development team, and as a foundation for system design, implementation, and testing.

#### 1.2 Project Scope
This project involves targeted enhancements to an existing Moodle installation to address critical gaps identified as barriers to replacing the legacy Blackboard system. The scope is limited to developing specific new functionalities and configurations without undertaking a full system rebuild or major architectural changes.

**In-Scope Enhancements:**
*   Multiple file upload capability for assignments, forums, and other configurable pages.
*   Audio recording and portfolio management tools tailored for language learning.
*   Global search functionality with filtering across all course materials.
*   Enhanced gradebook with grading, feedback, and audit history.
*   Configurable RSS web feed integration for dynamic content updates.

**Out-of-Scope Items:**
*   Replacement of Moodle's native social/collaborative tools (e.g., forums, messaging).
*   Development of a new courseware system architecture.
*   Major modifications to core Moodle APIs or database schema.
*   Integration with external social media platforms (e.g., Facebook, Twitter).
*   Comprehensive UI/UX overhaul of existing Moodle interfaces.

#### 1.3 Definitions, Acronyms, and Abbreviations
*   **API:** Application Programming Interface
*   **LMS:** Learning Management System
*   **RSS:** Really Simple Syndication (or Rich Site Summary)
*   **UI/UX:** User Interface / User Experience
*   **OIS:** Office of Information Services (University of Puget Sound)
*   **SRS:** Software Requirements Specification

#### 1.4 References
*   Moodle Official Documentation (https://docs.moodle.org/)
*   University of Puget Sound IT Standards and Practices
*   Stakeholder Interview Summaries (Internal Document)

#### 1.5 Document Overview
This document is structured to present an overall description of the product, followed by specific functional and non-functional requirements, and concluding with appendices for supplementary information.

### 2. Overall Description

#### 2.1 Product Perspective
This project is an enhancement module for the existing Moodle LMS. It will operate as a set of integrated plugins and configurations that extend the core Moodle functionality. The system must interoperate seamlessly with the existing Moodle core, authentication system, and database.

#### 2.2 User Classes and Characteristics
| User Class | Characteristics | Key Needs |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Student** | Primary end-user. Varying technical proficiency. Needs intuitive access to materials and submission tools. | Submit assignments, access content, receive grades/feedback, track personal progress (e.g., language portfolio). |
| **Professor (Instructor)** | Content creator and course manager. Moderate to high technical proficiency. Needs efficient course administration tools. | Upload materials, create activities, configure features (uploads, RSS), grade assignments, provide feedback. |
| **System Administrator** | Technical expert. Responsible for system health, security, and configuration. Limited availability (per constraints). | Install/configure plugins, manage backups, monitor performance, apply updates with minimal disruption. |

#### 2.3 Operating Environment
*   **Software:** Existing Moodle installation (version to be specified), standard LAMP/LEMP stack (Linux, Apache/Nginx, MySQL/MariaDB, PHP).
*   **Hardware:** University-hosted servers meeting Moodle's recommended specifications for ~1,000 concurrent users.
*   **Network:** Accessible via university network and VPN, with 24/7 availability expectations.

#### 2.4 Design and Implementation Constraints
1.  **API Constraint:** Enhancements must utilize existing Moodle plugin APIs and hooks. Deep core modifications are prohibited.
2.  **Maintainability Constraint:** The system must be largely self-sustaining due to limited OIS staff. Plugins must be stable, well-documented, and easy to update.
3.  **Compliance Constraint:** All features must comply with University IT standards, accessibility guidelines (WCAG 2.1 AA), and FERPA data protection requirements.
4.  **Budget/Time Constraint:** Development is phased by priority. Priority 3 features are explicitly limited by timeline and budget.
5.  **Usability Constraint:** The interface for new features must be simple, intuitive, and responsive, maintaining consistency with the existing Moodle UI.

#### 2.5 Assumptions and Dependencies
*   **Assumption:** The University will proceed with Moodle as the primary LMS, pending the success of this enhancement project.
*   **Assumption:** Adequate server storage is available for audio files and increased backup frequency.
*   **Dependency:** Project success is dependent on the stability and compatibility of the underlying Moodle core version.
*   **Dependency:** Final requirements for backup schedules and storage are dependent on University policy finalization.

### 3. System Features and Requirements

#### 3.1 Feature 1: Configurable Multiple File Upload
**3.1.1 Description**
Professors shall be able to enable or disable multiple file uploads on a per-activity basis (e.g., Assignment, Forum). When enabled, students can upload more than one file in a single submission action.

**3.1.2 Functional Requirements**
| ID | Requirement | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **FR1.1** | The system shall provide a configuration setting ("Allow multiple files") within the setup form for Assignment and Forum activities. | High |
| **FR1.2** | When enabled, the student submission interface shall display a dynamic interface to add, remove, and preview multiple files before final submission. | High |
| **FR1.3** | The system shall validate total upload size against the existing course/activity upload limit. | High |
| **FR1.4** | The system shall display all submitted files to the professor in the grading interface. | High |

#### 3.2 Feature 2: Audio Recording & Language Portfolio
**3.2.1 Description**
Students, particularly in language courses, shall be able to record audio directly within Moodle and manage recordings in a personal portfolio to track progress over time.

**3.2.2 Functional Requirements**
| ID | Requirement | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **FR2.1** | The system shall provide an "Audio Record" button within relevant activity types (e.g., Assignment submission, dedicated Portfolio activity). | High |
| **FR2.2** | The recording interface shall use the browser's MediaDevices API to capture microphone input, with visual feedback (e.g., level meter, record/stop buttons). | High |
| **FR2.3** | The system shall allow students to play back, re-record, and save the audio clip in a standard format (e.g., MP3, WebM). | High |
| **FR2.4** | The system shall provide a "My Language Portfolio" view where students can see a timeline of all their saved recordings, tagged with course/activity and date. | Medium |

#### 3.3 Feature 3: Global Course Search
**3.3.1 Description**
Students and professors shall be able to search for text across all pages and resources within their enrolled courses, with results filterable by course, activity type, and date.

**3.3.2 Functional Requirements**
| ID | Requirement | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **FR3.1** | A persistent "Search all my courses" field shall be available in the main site header. | High |
| **FR3.2** | The search shall index content from course pages, labels, assignment descriptions, forum posts, and resource files (text content). | High |
| **FR3.3** | The results page shall display matches with context snippets, title, course name, and activity type. | High |
| **FR3.4** | The results page shall provide filters to narrow results by Course, Content Type (e.g., Assignment, PDF, Forum), and Date Range. | Medium |

#### 3.4 Feature 4: Enhanced Gradebook with Feedback & History
**3.4.1 Description**
The gradebook shall be enhanced to provide a robust interface for grading, delivering detailed feedback, and maintaining a viewable history of grade changes.

**3.4.2 Functional Requirements**
| ID | Requirement | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **FR4.1** | The grading interface shall allow professors to enter a grade, select from pre-defined comment quick-keys, and enter rich-text/multimedia feedback for each student submission. | High |
| **FR4.2** | The system shall maintain an immutable audit log of all grade entries and changes, including timestamp and user who made the change. | High |
| **FR4.3** | Professors shall be able to view the history/audit log for any student's grade from within the gradebook. | Medium |
| **FR4.4** | Students shall be able to view their grade and associated feedback on their "User report" view, with clear indication of when feedback was provided. | High |

#### 3.5 Feature 5: Configurable RSS Web Feeds
**3.5.1 Description**
Professors shall be able to configure and display RSS feeds from external sources (e.g., news sites, academic journals, blog) on their course homepage or within specific topic sections.

**3.5.2 Functional Requirements**
| ID | Requirement | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **FR5.1** | The system shall provide an "RSS Feed" activity module that can be added to any course section. | Medium |
| **FR5.2** | When adding the activity, the professor shall specify the RSS feed URL, number of items to display, and whether to show description/summary. | Medium |
| **FR5.3** | The system shall cache feed content to avoid excessive external requests and display it in a formatted block within the course. | Medium |
| **FR5.4** | Feed updates shall be refreshed according to a configurable system-wide cron schedule (e.g., every 60 minutes). | Low |

#### 3.6 Feature 6: Configurable Backup Scheduling
**3.6.1 Description**
System Administrators shall have a simplified, reliable interface to configure automated backup schedules for course data, with options for frequency and retention.

**3.6.2 Functional Requirements**
| ID | Requirement | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **FR6.1** | The system shall provide an administrative interface to set automated backup schedules (e.g., daily, weekly) for all courses or courses by category. | High |
| **FR6.2** | The administrator shall be able to configure retention policies (e.g., keep 4 weekly backups, 12 monthly backups). | Medium |
| **FR6.3** | The system shall generate logs for each backup operation, indicating success/failure and data size. | Medium |
| **FR6.4** | Backup files shall be stored in a designated, secure filesystem location accessible for potential off-site transfer (process TBD). | Medium |

### 4. Non-Functional Requirements

#### 4.1 Performance Requirements
*   **PR1:** The system shall support **1,000 concurrent users** with a page load time of under 3 seconds for core actions (browsing, submitting) during peak periods.
*   **PR2:** Search queries across all courses for a single user shall return results within **5 seconds**.
*   **PR3:** Audio recording shall initiate capture within **2 seconds** of user permission grant.

#### 4.2 Availability & Reliability
*   **AR1:** The overall system, including new features, shall achieve **99% uptime** excluding planned maintenance windows.
*   **AR2:** The system shall have a Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) of no less than 720 hours for newly developed components.

#### 4.3 Security & Compliance
*   **SC1:** All enhancements shall adhere to Moodle's native role-based permission system. No feature shall bypass these controls.
*   **SC2:** User-generated audio files shall be stored with permissions ensuring they are accessible only to the intended user, their professors, and system administrators.
*   **SC3:** The system shall maintain FERPA compliance, ensuring grade and feedback data is protected and auditable.

#### 4.4 Usability
*   **US1:** New configuration options for professors shall be located within the standard Moodle activity setup forms, following existing UI patterns.
*   **US2:** The interface for students to upload multiple files or record audio shall be learnable within 1 minute of first use, as validated by user testing.
*   **US3:** All new text and interfaces shall meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards.

#### 4.5 Maintainability & Support
*   **MS1:** All custom code shall be developed as discrete Moodle plugins, documented with inline comments and a README file explaining configuration.
*   **MS2:** The system shall be designed to allow for updates to the core Moodle version with minimal rework required for the enhancement plugins.

### 5. Appendices

#### Appendix A: User Stories Mapping to Requirements
| User Story | Mapped Requirement IDs |
| :--- | :--- |
| 1. Professor - Multiple file uploads | FR1.1, FR1.2, FR1.4 |
| 2. Language Student - Audio portfolio | FR2.1, FR2.2, FR2.3, FR2.4 |
| 3. Student - Search across courses | FR3.1, FR3.2, FR3.3 |
| 4. Professor - RSS feeds for announcements | FR5.1, FR5.2, FR5.3 |
| 5. Professor - Grade with feedback | FR4.1, FR4.4 |
| 6. SysAdmin - Configurable backups | FR6.1, FR6.2, FR6.3 |

#### Appendix B: Success Metrics Verification
*   **Metric 1 (1000 concurrent users):** Verified via load testing scripts simulating peak activity mix.
*   **Metric 2 (99% Uptime):** Monitored via institutional network monitoring tools (e.g., Nagios) over a 6-month post-launch period.
*   **Metric 3 (Priority 1 & 2 Implementation):** Verified via Requirement Traceability Matrix and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) sign-off on all High-priority requirements.

#### Appendix C: Open/Undecided Issues
1.  The implementation approach for wiki/blog integration (a Priority 3 feature) is deferred. Options include using existing Moodle plugins or limited custom development.
2.  Final institutional commitment to Moodle adoption is pending the successful delivery and evaluation of this project.
3.  Exact backup frequency (e.g., daily vs. weekly) and off-site storage protocol require final policy approval from University administration.
4.  The design for a unified notification subscription manager (beyond RSS) is deferred to a potential future phase.
5.  The approach for developing comprehensive end-user documentation (guides, videos) will be determined post-development, based on available resources.

---
*Document End*
